name: PLAY BALL!
notes: 60 feet 6 inches, best-of-seven Series and Cooperstown as an upstate NY village all correct; clean rules-to-lore climb, no player names to age out.

name: BOYS OF SUMMER
notes: Verified Paige's 1948 Cleveland debut at 42; Aaron 1974, Mays' 1954 catch, Berra quote and Williams' .406 all solid and every figure is safely historical.

name: IN THIS CORNER
notes: Verified Joe Louis' 1937-1949 reign; Thrilla in Manila 1975, Walker Smith Jr. and Dempsey-Tunney 1926 all accurate; evergreen and warm for the target player.

name: GOING FOR THE GOLD
notes: Verified Retton at 16 with the perfect-10 vault in 1984 and Hamill's 1976 wedge; Spitz's seven golds and the Miracle on Ice correct — Hamill at $1000 is no harder than Retton at $800.

name: PICK A CARD, ANY CARD
notes: 52-card deck, face cards worth 10 at blackjack, Old Maid, two-handed gin rummy and the royal flush all accurate; gin's juniper hook is the standout.

name: BACKYARD CHAMPIONS
notes: Ladder never climbed — jacks at $1000 is a gimme for this audience; swapped it for bocce and its pallino, giving the top row a real but still-warm step up.

name: GONE FISHIN'
notes: Bobber, reel, rainbow/brook trout, shanty ice fishing all correct; the bass homograph makes a fun, unambiguous $1000.

name: HAPPY CAMPERS
notes: All five accurate; 'leaves of three' also fits poison oak, but 'woodland vine' steers it to ivy, and merit badges are correctly round and sash-worn.

name: SWING YOUR PARTNER
notes: Verified Arthur Murray's mail-order numbered-footprint lessons; square dance caller, 3/4-time waltz, tango and Virginia reel all correct — no overlap with e2-golden's CUTTING A RUG dance crazes.

name: RIGHT UP YOUR ALLEY
notes: Strike/spare marks, twelve strikes for 300, hook into the pocket and the 7-10 split all accurate; best genuine climb in the file.

name: THE HOBBY SHOP
notes: $200 'stamps' and $1000 'philately' were the same hobby twice, telegraphing the finisher — replaced $1000 with genealogy; $600 steel-penny clue also reframed as a coin-collecting clue for category fit.

name: RACK 'EM UP
notes: Cue chalk, eight ball, the break's fifteen-ball rack, scratch and snooker's 15 reds plus six colors all correct; tidy jargon ladder.
